title: eval-harness: integrate per-prompt regression metrics into CI hooks and quality gating
author: Leah Morgan
release_notes: Add per-prompt regression metrics to eval-harness CI hooks and quality gating. CI will now surface per-prompt false-positive/false-negative regressions and block merges if thresholds are exceeded. Includes new metrics exporter, tests, and docs.
body: Context: Teams have been requesting finer-grained regression signals for prompt-set based evaluations so that a small aggregate improvement doesn’t mask regressions on critical prompts. This PR adds per-prompt metrics to the eval-harness CI hooks and wires them into the quality-gating config so the CI can fail on localized regressions beyond configured thresholds. What this changes: - New per-prompt metrics exporter (precision/recall/f1/delta) emitted by the eval runner. - CI hook that computes per-prompt deltas between baseline and candidate runs and applies configurable thresholds. - Quality gating configuration (eval-harness/config/quality_gates.yaml) with per-prompt thresholds and opt-in allowlists. - Unit and integration tests for metric calculation and CI behavior. - Documentation and a short migration note for teams that consume eval artifacts. Why: Currently our CI pages report only aggregated metrics. Several recent regressions were caught late because regressions on small but important prompts were lost in aggregate averages. This gives teams an actionable, automated gate to avoid regressions on priority prompts. Implementation notes: - The metrics exporter is implemented as eval-harness/ci/hooks/per_prompt_metrics.py and uses the existing eval result schema; it emits a per_prompt.metrics JSON blob alongside aggregate.metrics. - The CI hook (eval-harness/ci/hooks/quality_gate_runner.py) now calls the per-prompt comparator and interprets thresholds from config/quality_gates.yaml. The comparator supports absolute delta and relative-percent thresholds. - Backwards compatibility: if no per-prompt thresholds are configured, behavior is unchanged. - Tests: eval-harness/tests/test_per_prompt_metrics.py and test_quality_gate_integration.py cover calculation and CI decision trees. - Docs: docs/eval-harness/ci.md updated with configuration examples and a troubleshooting section. Checklist: - [x] Add exporter and comparator logic - [x] Add tests covering edge cases (missing prompts, NaNs) - [x] Wire into CI hooks - [x] Docs and migration guidance - [x] Performance sanity check (added minimal parsing overhead) Related: ENG-2345 (design doc), ENG-2401 (follow-up request for dashboarding per-prompt trends). Links: linear.redwoodapp.com/ENG-2345 CI notes: Initial CI run failed on a flaky timing test in test_quality_gate_integration; fixed by making the test deterministic (stubbed time). All other checks pass. Merge strategy: squash-merge to keep a single logical change for revertability.

review_comments: Tomás Vega: Please add an allowlist mechanism so customers can opt prompts out of gating; also make sure thresholds can be expressed per-priority-tag.
Leah Morgan: Added allowlist and per-priority threshold fields to quality_gates.yaml; documented behavior in CI docs.
Samir Gupta: The comparator looks good but can we reduce memory footprint for very large prompt-sets? Consider streaming comparison instead of holding full arrays.
Leah Morgan: Switched comparator to a streaming reducer; memory usage dropped in local perf tests from ~200MB to ~30MB on a 50k-prompt run.
Priya Nair: CI failure mode: please ensure failure messages include prompt id and short diff summary to help triage.
Leah Morgan: CI now emits a top-k worst prompts list with metric deltas and a link to the full per_prompt.metrics artifact.
Tomás Vega: Approved on green CI. (approval)
